items.title: 2027 campaigns: More details needed, by Tonnie Iredia
items.description: Immediately after the 2023 general elections, many politicians began illegal electioneering campaigns for the next set of elections scheduled for 2027. All efforts to remind them that they were abandoning governance which is the real essence of democracy and which should naturally follow elections failed. The truth however is that those cosmetic gestures across the nation made up of political alignments and defections which are essentially self-seeking do not constitute proper campaigns. Politicians with great ideas of how to improve the living standards of the people ought to be better disposed. They ought not to jump the gun by engaging in premature campaigns just as whatever campaigns they choose to participate in at the appropriate time should be detailed enough to aptly enlighten the people to make informed choices. Now that campaigns have rightly begun, politicians must not be allowed to be sleepy, instead they are obliged to educate us all on their manifestoes and election promises. It is against this backdrop that we call on all politicians to embrace issue-based campaigns and also to put an end to the practice of taking our citizens for granted. In the last one week, Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC appears to have gained some traction even without supplying us with all the details concerning the political messages he has fired. First, Atiku says if elected, he would restore fuel subsidy. The loud applause which greeted the promise does not mean that people understood how the maker intends to fulfil the promise. Ordinarily, considering the high level of corruption which surrounded subsidy since 1999 when the same Atiku was the nation’s vice president, a persuasive analysis of how he intends to accomplish the goal is what should deserve an applause but many people are excited because the candidate’s message suits the emotions of the moment. Atiku and his principal, Olusegun Obasanjo were in power from 1999 to 2007; they could not defeat the oil thieves that were described as a cartel by government. From then till 2023, successive governments established beyond reasonable doubt that the cartel was invincible. If Atiku is elected in 2027 and he restores subsidy, the cartel and fuel scarcity may return but at this point only a few would bother about that because it concerns the future. At the peak of the Obasanjo-Atiku presidency, fuel price moved to N49 per litre thereby raising huge inflation of prices across the board. The hard-fighting Nigerian Labour Congress NLC of those days tackled the government. Federal and state officials and indeed the national council of states came up with a solution for each state to provide N200million naira to which the federal government was to donate N100m per state for the purchase of buses to be given to transporters to bring down the high cost of transportation at the time. Whereas the federal government met its own side of the arrangement, I think it was only Lagos and Oyo states that released their own counterpart funding. In short, the lofty idea eventually failed making it clear that as soon as some truce is achieved on a subject, government has a way of giving up on its promises. What this suggests is that it is unwise to trust politicians concerning the people’s welfare. Now that people are clapping for the likely return of subsidy, we expect the ruling party to task Atiku to give details of his plan to return the nation to what hurt us before. Meanwhile, no one knows if what Atiku is championing will be better or worse. Indeed, what evidence is there that Atiku is not only looking for how to get into power? When did he discover the strategy, he wants to unfold now? While some people would see him as unpatriotic if he has always known it but chose to hoard it as a joker to be pulled up only when he comes to power, others would not trust the efficacy of the strategy if it was recently hurriedly designed to capture power. All of that is politics. What matters is that everyone will be forced to communicate; some may have to publish and translate their own viewpoint into several local languages because Nigerians have had cause not to trust any group that have at one time or the other constituted the governments of their country. In the case of the 2027 elections, not all Nigerians would be simplistic enough to accept slogans as election promises. If many people are unhappy with the result of ‘subsidy is gone’ why would most people not be more irritated if ‘I will bring back subsidy’ takes us back to the dark old days when no one knew the quantity of oil produced per day in Nigeria or even the number of trucks loaded per day or their destinations. Nigeria’s civic society should grow up. The same respected presidential candidate has come up with another well-sounding statement namely that if elected into office in 2027, he would reopen all closed borders. His main argument that trans-border trade is a legitimate business has a point but can that alone be the basis for opening or closing borders? Theoretically, it can be argued that the closure of the borders of a country can hurt the economic interests of many trans-border traders. Consequently, opening the borders may have some advantages. There is doubt however if Atiku’s conclusion that the borders were unreasonably closed is correct. As a matter of fact, there is no evidence that the borders were still closed at the point the ADC candidate was promising to open them when elected. This is because some few hours after Atiku’s statement on border closure, the presidency countered him. According to Sunday Dare, the President’s Special Adviser on Media and Public Communication, ‘the federal government had reopened most of the country’s land borders in March 2024 and had not reversed the policy.’ He therefore questioned the basis of Atiku’s pledge, asking which borders the ADC presidential candidate intended to open when the existing policy already permits legitimate movement and trade. The truth is that because our leaders are fond of taking us for granted Nigerians did not know whether our borders had been opened or closed. The little we all know consists of several controversies attributable to liberal policies concerning national borders. There is the issue of smuggling which reportedly increased when borders were left open without control. More importantly, not many Nigerians would be excited over the opening of borders considering the complexities of herder-farmer conflicts which assumed greater proportions following the influx of migrants in the days of free movement and visa on arrival policy in Nigeria. We all had to be admonished to avoid ethnic profiling and to recognize that all Fulani are not the same. Under the circumstance, no politician should resort to these sensitive issues without properly stating the details of his intention especially the arrangements he has designed for dealing with their effects. We welcome the quick response by the presidency to Atiku’s statements which have since affected the reaction of some groups. The ensuing discussions have clearly established the importance of political debates which when properly organized can help our people to be better educated in making informed decisions. It is too late in the day considering our nation’s stunted growth to allow our politicians to continue to take the people for granted. It is therefore hoped that in the days ahead, all our politicians will imbibe the spirit of political debates which are integral to the presidential system of government. As stated earlier, the ADC candidate has to be more forthcoming. His absence at the recent outing of major presidential candidates in Port Harcourt under the auspices of the Nigerian Bar Association was a minus more so as his vice, Rotimi Amaechi who was present made us believe that he was yet to be on the same page as his principal. Similarly, the incumbent president, Bola Ahmed Tinubu was also absent. In Nigeria, handlers of incumbents are fond of making the same mistake that their candidate should be absent so as to avoid being the target. The posture is wrong because during a debate, he is essentially a presidential candidate seeking votes like all others. Bearing in mind that meeting the media, facing the camera and addressing a large audience are not Tinubu’s weaknesses, it is an error of judgment on the part of his handlers to talk him out of any presidential debate. In a properly moderated debate, a seasoned anchor will give no room for anyone to be targeted. Everyone should be free to appropriately brief all voters. It is time for Nigeria to be a communicating nation. The post 2027 campaigns: More details needed, by Tonnie Iredia appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Prepare to get results, by Funmi Komolafe
items.description: Let’s begin by giving glory to God that we are alive to witness the last Sunday in the month of August. Lamentations 3 vs. 22 ( KJV) “ It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because its compassions fail not”. Beloved, you and I are beneficiaries of the Lord’s mercy and compassion. As the month of August commonly called the month of a “ New Beginning”, winds down, we should be prepared to testify to a new beginning. A new beginning begins with new results that make one glad. If a student has been writing exams without success and he writes one that propels him into excellence, certainly he’ll be happy as he begins to experience a new beginning. However, the student must have done something. He probably devoted more time to his studies and prayer sessions. These two activities would bring to manifestation in this life, the word of the God in Deuteronomy 28 vs. 12 : “ The LORD shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow”. The emphasis for us here is “ to bless all the work of thine hand”. Brethren, blessings may not come when we do nothing. You have to do something to get something beyond your expectation from God. It therefore means that you must prepare for blessings to be blessed. Results may never come when you refuse to prepare for it but when it comes, it ushers a season of joy. Indeed a new beginning. When one experiences a challenge, that person is likely to be a subject of insults from mockers . The attitude of such a person isn’t to fight back with insults , rather, it is to go to the Lord in prayer with a simply prayer point. “ O God cancel every insult in my life”. This simple prayer made in faith regularly, would produce results in Jesus name. You cannot afford to give up when you haven’t gotten results even when you get results you still need prayers to sustain and retain that miracle. Psalm 37 vs. 5 tells us : “Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass”. To commit your ways unto the LORD is to make a conscious effort to build your spiritual capacity with prayers, worship, thanksgiving and service to God. This, is a personal decision that you have to make. I’ll share the testimony of a lady who was waiting on the Lord after many years of marriage. She began to confess the word of God in Deuteronomy 7 vs. 14: “ Thou shalt be blessed above all people: there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle”. She regularly repeated these Bible verse in a day. Someone saw her walking and talking. The person called her husband and asked, “ Is anything wrong with your wife? I saw your wife walking and talking to herself”. Her husband told the person that his wife is perfectly okay . It was not long after she started the daily and regular confession of the word that the she conceived. Brethren, to get a result, you must meditate on the word of God regularly. Not only that, you need to memorise the Bible passage that address the challenge you want out of your life. For instance a lawyer that goes to a judge without making reference to any judicial precedence or what the law says about a case will never win a case. To be a winner, you must prepare for results. In the case of the woman mentioned earlier, after conception, she changed her prayer point with Exodus 23 vs. 26: “ There shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren, in thy land; the number of thy days I will fulfill”. With these words of God, she laminated her self and the baby in her against all attacks of the enemy. At the appropriate time she gave birth to a set of triplets. She prepared for results and God gave her more than she expected. Brethren, those who do not sow do not harvest. The season of harvest is the time of results, it is the time of joy and celebration. It is the time that the farmer forgets hard labour that has been put into farm work. For other persons, it is the time to put the trauma of challenges behind. May God help us overcome all challenges in Jesus name. So what do results bring for us as believers? Results, here refers to miracles that we expect from God. For a woman called barren like Sarah, Hannah and Rachael, the result that would cancel insults in her life is the birth of a child. 1st Samuel 1 verses 19 &20 : “ And they rose up in the morning early , and worshipped before the LORD, and returned, and came to their house in Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her”. Note that Hannah prepared for a miracle by pouring out her heart to the LORD in prayer and made a vow. You make a vow when you believe that the prayer would be answered. It takes a high level of faith to make a vow. Verse 20: “ Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD”. Brethren, you get what you desire from the LORD provided you also prepare for it. Healing is another result that can cancel insult. A person held down with sickness is likely to be the subject of insults from those that pretend to pity him. Brethren may the LORD open our spiritual eyes to see beyond the physical. It is not all manifestations of illness that are physical. Some have spiritual origins. Our father in the Lord, Daddy Enoch Adeboye once said, if you do all tests and doctors see nothing and you remain unwell, you should realize that the problem is spiritual. Therefore, you need to turn to Jesus pleading for mercy . This prayer point is recommended. “Merciful father, please remove every hand of the enemy on my health and make me whole”. There is a promise of God for us in Exodus 15 vs. 26: “ And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and will give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statues, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that healeth thee”. These words are further sealed with the word, in Isaiah 53 vs. 5: “ But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed” Prepare and claim your right in the LORD. It shall be well. The post Prepare to get results, by Funmi Komolafe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Will the Judiciary condone forgery? By Dele Sobowale
items.description: “Let justice be done, though the heavens fall” – Lord Mansfield, 1705-1793 “Once to every man and nation comes the moment to decide; in the strife of truth with falsehood, for the good or evil side” – James Russell Lowell, 1819-1891 Until now, there was no reason to raise the question about substantial justice untainted with legal subterfuges – like the Supreme Court decision which declared a fourth place finisher in an election the winner; after awarding him more votes than INEC announced were counted. The Nigerian judiciary, since that judgment, had steadily reduced public confidence in the Third Estate of the Realm. We are in the season again when justice would be tested to the limit. But, it is not only magistrates and “Your Lordships” who will be on trial before the entire world and posterity. Every Nigerian taking a position on this matter, in the court of public opinion is also on trial. Our ethical standards are on display as well. Each one of us is being asked to declare our position on alleged forgery and doubtful particulars – as well as omissions of relevant facts. I am aware that: “Money makes everything legitimate, including bastards” (Jewish proverb). But, for once, for the sake of our nation, we should not allow ourselves to be swayed by money or appointments. Only by facts. One Federal High Court Justice already ruffled feathers by pronouncing on a matter before the Court of Appeal. Was it human error or willful judicial rascality? If a genuine mistake was made, then, decency demanded that the judge should have publicly apologised. If the measure was deliberate, the obvious questions are: Was it induced? What induced it? As the late Chief MKO Abiola would say: “Nobody stands all day in the rain for nothing”. Insults have rained down on the judge ever since. Since our return to civil rule in 1999, alleged forged certificates have been revealed in every election by contestants for various offices. And virtually all the known claims of forged or dodgy credentials have ended the same way. The candidate was dismissed by the courts – giving the impression that the Nigerian judiciary would not condone anybody benefiting from illegality. That was noble of the judges who handled those cases. ALL CANDIDATES ARE EQUAL. ARE SOME MORE EQUAL THAN OTHERS? “Laws are like cobwebs where the small flies are caught; and the great breakthrough” – Francis Bacon, 1561-1626 China recently jailed, for life, the founder of one of the biggest real estate businesses the world has ever known – the EVERGRANDE – on account of fraud. At the peak of its success, the company employed over 150,000 people directly or indirectly. The convict was a dollar billionaire. But, China is a nation with zero tolerance for corruption. That was how it climbed to become the second biggest economic and military power globally. The case lasted less than six months. In Nigeria, a combination of ruling party politicians, EFCC, selfish and unpatriotic Senior Advocates of Nigeria, and, above all, dishonourable justices would have ensured that the case languishes in court for years; or is inevitably concluded on terms favourable to the accused. One Prince Ajudua is still being tried for crimes allegedly committed more than 20 years ago even as about six sitting senators have their case files gathering dust in the EFCC office right now. Obviously, Nigerians, including some of our chief law officers, regularly condone lawlessness – if those involved are friends and benefactors. “The law, in its majestic equality, forbids the rich as well as the poor to sleep under bridges, to beg on the streets and to steal bread” – Anatole France, 1844-1924. Meanwhile, our judges waste no time sending poor offenders to jail for petty theft. In the time it had taken the cases against some senators to be bottled up, hundreds of thousands of poor Nigerians have been sentenced for stealing as little as a small goat. Collectively, Nigerians have extended that ethical duplicity to politics. A member of the House of Representatives, representing a northern state, is kicked out and prosecuted for certificate forgery; and the people of Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Osun, Ondo and Ekiti endorse the decision. Then a Lagos politician is accused of certificate forgery; suddenly, the same people are asking Nigerians to ignore the crime; for the judiciary to throw out the case and well-paid SANs have been lined up to ensure that their client gets away with unethical and illegal conduct. The judiciary is once again put on trial. WILL NIGERIA AND THE JUDICIARY CONTINUE TO ENDORSE FORGERY? “To be or not to be? That is the question.” William Shakespeare, 1564-1616, in Nigeria is at crossroads regarding whether we want to create a nation like the Nordic nations which, though smaller in size and population as well as lacking natural resources, have far greater Gross Domestic Productivity, GDP, than us. Or the giants, China, India and Brazil, blessed with population, landmass and natural resources; which have been used to propel them to the top 20 economies; instead of remaining mired in poverty. All the leading nations have enjoyed good leadership; defined as a combination of intelligence and integrity. Nobody can become the Prime Minister of India or President of China – whose entire life history is unknown. Open any search engine and the true life history – birth, father’s and mother’s names, primary and secondary schools, university attended, work experience etc – of the German Chancellor is revealed. Nothing is hidden. Consult the same search engine; ask for information about some leaders of Nigeria. The yawning gaps in the life history of some of the leaders of Africa’s most populated nation explain more eloquently than an entire book why Nigeria lags behind tiny Singapore in GDP – as well as per capita income. The integrity gap between Nigerian leaders and those of other nations represents the missing variable. Can anybody imagine a candidate for Mayor of New York City, NYC, leaving out of his application form the names of his primary and secondary schools; and a State High Court deciding in his favour if his candidacy is contested? Why would someone deliberately omit information, which every other applicant for elective office has provided – for verification? Is concealment of fraud intended by the omission? Nigerian courts – State High, Federal High, Appeal Courts and the Supreme Courts of Nigeria -might soon be asked to answer that question. DOES CHARACTER MATTER TO NIGERIANS ANYMORE? “A precedent embalms a principle” – Lord Stowell, 1745-1836. Whether we like it or not, Nigeria has a truth problem confronting us in the coming 2027 elections. It might be the time we finally decide as a nation if certificate forgery is acceptable for all elections, some elections or no elections. We are not only confronted with pre-meditated omissions of vital information; even the certificates presented are being challenged as fake. Then, there is the lingering matter of hundreds of thousands of dollars voluntarily forfeited to the US government during an alleged shady past; and, curiously, the US Federal Bureau of Investigations, FBI, has stubbornly refused to release information concerning the matter. Silence sometimes tells a lot more than intended. When a globally respected crime fighting organization refuses to disclose information about an alleged crime, it only deepens suspicion. Nobody can make me give up one dollar; because it would have been earned legitimately; throwing away hundreds of thousands of dollars should be out of the question – for a man whose hands are clean. Obviously, we are not only being asked to forgive a suspicious omission of facts. We are also being requested to overlook the possibility of certificate forgery. Worst of all, we are collectively supposed to endorse the likelihood of illicit drug dealership – despite its documented destructive impacts on nations; including Nigeria. In that case, why not start by scrapping the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA? When a clown becomes king or queen, the palace becomes a circus. What happens when a suspected drug Lord ascends the throne? We are being asked to determine whether to continue to condone alleged questionable deeds. Nigerians, in general, and the judiciary in particular, will have a choice before or in 2027. Everyone of us must bear in mind, as we cast our votes, that we will be affirming one principle or another. We could continue to promote corruption – in all its ramifications; or, we could decide, at last, to emulate those nations which have adopted zero tolerance as state policy. “Wisdom in people consists of the anticipation of consequences” – Norman Cousins, 1915-1990. Africans are the slowest learners on Earth. It is not an accident that our continent is also the most backward. Corruption is believed to be more widely accepted here than anywhere else; even in the judiciary. We have experienced the consequences of having dubious leaders. Can we stop? That is the question. Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola The post Will the Judiciary condone forgery? By Dele Sobowale appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Exportations : 37,3 milliards de dollars de potentiel pour le Maroc à l’horizon 2031
items.description: Le potentiel d’exportation du Maroc sur les marchés avec lesquels il entretient déjà des relations commerciales pourrait atteindre 37,3 milliards de dollars à l’horizon 2031, selon une analyse du cabinet indien 6WResearch . Les États-Unis concentreraient à eux seuls 10,76 milliards de dollars de cette réserve de croissance, devant la Chine, le Japon et l’Inde. À ce montant pourraient s’ajouter 10,17 milliards de dollars liés à de nouveaux couples produit-marché. Le potentiel d’exportation du Maroc pourrait changer d’échelle au cours des prochaines années. Selon une analyse de 6WResearch , les ventes susceptibles d’être réalisées en 2031 sur des marchés où les produits marocains sont déjà présents représentent une enveloppe de 37,3 milliards de dollars, soit environ 345,1 milliards de dirhams. Ce montant ne constitue pas une prévision du niveau des exportations en 2031. Il correspond à une estimation des marges de croissance encore disponibles sur les marchés existants, à partir notamment de la demande des pays importateurs et des positions commerciales déjà établies. Les États-Unis constituent le principal réservoir de croissance identifié par le cabinet indien. Sur les 37,3 milliards de dollars recensés, 10,76 milliards sont associés au marché américain, soit 28,85% du total. La Chine arrive loin derrière avec 4,40 milliards de dollars, suivie du Japon avec 2,44 milliards, de l’Inde avec 2,41 milliards et du Canada avec 2 milliards. Ces cinq marchés concentrent ainsi près de 59% de la réserve de croissance identifiée. Le potentiel américain apparaît d’autant plus important qu’il contraste avec le niveau actuel des échanges. D’après les données américaines reprises dans l’analyse, les importations de marchandises marocaines ont atteint 1,86 milliard de dollars en 2025. Le montant théorique identifié pour 2031 représente donc près de six fois la valeur enregistrée cette année-là. Automobile et engrais concentrent les principales marges de croissance L’analyse fait ressortir une forte concentration sectorielle. Les faisceaux électriques destinés à l’industrie automobile constituent le premier gisement identifié, avec un potentiel de 4,64 milliards de dollars. Les États-Unis en représenteraient 2,31 milliards, devant le Japon avec 838,47 millions de dollars. Les engrais forment le deuxième grand pilier de cette réserve de croissance. Le potentiel associé aux engrais au phosphate d’ammonium est estimé à 2,28 milliards de dollars, tandis que celui des engrais azotés et potassiques atteint 2,18 milliards. Le Brésil apparaît comme le principal débouché pour le premier segment, avec 927,82 millions de dollars, alors que l’Inde concentrerait 1,11 milliard de dollars du potentiel lié au second. L’électronique complète ce tableau. Les circuits intégrés logiques présentent un potentiel de 1,82 milliard de dollars, principalement porté par la Chine. Les petites voitures à essence représentent pour leur part 1,80 milliard de dollars, avec une demande particulièrement importante en Arabie saoudite. À eux seuls, les cinq principaux segments recensés sur les marchés déjà exploités totalisent 12,71 milliards de dollars. Cette répartition montre que l’essentiel des marges de croissance repose d’abord sur des filières déjà implantées dans l’industrie exportatrice, plutôt que sur l’émergence immédiate de secteurs entièrement nouveaux. Cette lecture permet également de relativiser le poids des États-Unis dans l’ensemble du commerce extérieur. L’Europe reste de très loin le principal socle des relations commerciales existantes. L’Espagne, la France et l’Allemagne figurent parmi les principaux marchés recensés par 6WResearch , avec respectivement 18,21 milliards, 15,84 milliards et 4,40 milliards de dollars d’exportations. Le marché américain apparaît ainsi davantage comme un levier de diversification que comme un substitut aux débouchés européens. L’accord de libre-échange entre les deux pays, en vigueur depuis 2006, constitue néanmoins un atout structurel pour une éventuelle progression des ventes. Les exportateurs disposent déjà d’un cadre commercial préférentiel, ce qui place les États-Unis parmi les marchés où une augmentation des flux peut s’appuyer sur des relations existantes. 10,17 milliards de dollars liés à de nouveaux débouchés Au-delà des marchés déjà exploités, 6WResearch identifie une seconde enveloppe de 10,17 milliards de dollars correspondant à des couples produit-marché encore inexistants ou faiblement développés. Les États-Unis arrivent là encore en tête, avec 2,69 milliards de dollars, soit 26,46% du total. Le Mexique suit avec 800 millions de dollars, devant la Chine avec 680 millions, puis le Japon et l’Inde avec environ 570 millions chacun. L’automobile et les technologies qui lui sont associées dominent cette deuxième catégorie d’opportunités. Les voitures à essence de moyenne cylindrée constituent le principal segment, avec 1,08 milliard de dollars de potentiel. Le marché américain en représenterait 523,29 millions, contre 335,91 millions pour l’Arabie saoudite. Les voitures particulières à essence de 1,5 à 3 litres représentent ensuite 418,23 millions de dollars, dont 353,33 millions pour les États-Unis. Les batteries lithium-ion ajoutent 357,41 millions de dollars, avec une demande potentielle américaine évaluée à 165,94 millions. Les véhicules électriques représentent pour leur part 311,28 millions de dollars. Ces perspectives s’inscrivent dans la montée en puissance de l’écosystème automobile et électrique. 6WResearch cite notamment les projets de Gotion High-Tech, BTR, CNGR-Al Mada, Hailiang et Shinzoom, qui doivent contribuer à développer une chaîne industrielle autour des batteries et des véhicules électriques. À l’échelle de l’ensemble des opportunités recensées, les batteries et les véhicules électriques restent toutefois des segments encore secondaires. Leur intérêt tient surtout à l’évolution de la structure des exportations, avec l’apparition progressive de produits à plus forte intensité technologique aux côtés des véhicules thermiques, des faisceaux électriques et des engrais. La même logique concerne les phosphates. 6WResearch estime à 4,46 milliards de dollars le potentiel associé aux engrais au phosphate d’ammonium ainsi qu’aux engrais azotés et potassiques. Cette perspective intervient alors que le groupe OCP prévoit de porter sa capacité de production d’engrais d’environ 12 millions à 20 millions de tonnes par an à l’horizon 2027. La question centrale reste donc celle de la transformation de ce potentiel théorique en échanges effectifs. L’analyse du cabinet indien s’appuie sur la demande des pays importateurs, les échanges bilatéraux, les structures tarifaires et d’autres variables économiques pour identifier les marges de progression possibles. La concrétisation de ces opportunités dépendra ensuite de facteurs beaucoup plus concrets : capacités industrielles disponibles, entrée en production des nouvelles unités, homologations, signature de contrats commerciaux, intégration aux chaînes de valeur mondiales et évolution des conditions douanières. items.title: Niger : une importante base militaire reprise après des affrontements à Niamey
items.description: Le régime militaire du Niger a repris samedi soir, avec l'aide de son partenaire russe, une importante base militaire de la capitale, Niamey, qui était aux mains de mutins depuis le début de la journée. « La garde présidentielle a repris le contrôle de la base aérienne avec l'aide des Russes. Il y a plusieurs morts dans les rangs des mutins », a indiqué une source diplomatique à Niamey. La reprise de la base a été confirmée par deux sources sécuritaires. Des échanges de tirs à l'arme lourde ont eu lieu dans la nuit et la matinée dans plusieurs quartiers de la capitale, dont la zone de la présidence et celle de l'aéroport où se trouve la base militaire 101, point névralgique du régime, entre des soldats mutins et ceux restés loyaux, notamment la garde présidentielle. « La garde présidentielle a repris le contrôle de la base aérienne avec l'aide des Russes. Il y a plusieurs morts dans les rangs des mutins », a indiqué à l'AFP une source diplomatique à Niamey. La reprise de la base a été confirmée par deux sources sécuritaires, l'une d'elles évoquant « la fin de la mutinerie ». L'ambassadeur de Russie à Niamey, Viktor Voropaïev cité par l'agence publique russe Sputnik Afrique avait affirmé un peu plus tôt que le Niger avait sollicité l'aide du groupe paramilitaire russe Africa Corps « pour réprimer une mutinerie ». Les éléments d'Africa Corps ont leur quartier général au sein de la base 101, qui héberge également l'état-major de la force unifiée de l'Alliance des Etats du Sahel (AES), la confédération que le Niger forme avec le Burkina Faso et le Mali. Selon deux sources diplomatiques de la région, interrogées avant la reprise de la base 101, des éléments des forces armées nigériennes convergeaient samedi, notamment depuis Ouallam au nord de Niamey, vers la capitale, sans que l'on sache quel camp ils comptaient rallier. Dans la matinée, le ministre de la Défense Salifou Mody avait assuré dans un communiqué que l'armée reprenait progressivement le contrôle face à un « groupe de soldats en rupture avec le règlement militaire » qui avaient séquestré « certains de leurs camarades dans la caserne de la base 101 de Niamey » et tiré sur plusieurs « sites sensibles » de la ville. Mais dans l'après-midi les mutins, dont les revendications restent inconnues, occupaient encore trois casernes, dont celle de la base 101. Dans le centre-ville où se trouve le palais présidentiel, le calme était revenu en fin de matinée, selon des riverains. Les accès à la présidence et la télévision nationale sont toutefois bouclés par un fort dispositif militaire. Et pour se rendre à la base aérienne, les deux voies d'accès sont également bloquées, l'une par des pneus posés en travers de la chaussée. items.title: Akufo-Addo praises Dagbon for upholding Peace Accord
items.description: Former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo has commended the Dagbon Traditional Council for maintaining the Peace Accord following the death of the late Ya-Na Abukari II. He said the decision by the Regent and senior traditional leaders to uphold the accord demonstrated their commitment to preserving the peace that had been painstakingly restored in Dagbon. Nana Akufo-Addo made the remarks when he visited the Gbewaa Palace in Yendi on Saturday, August 29, to commiserate with the Regent of Dagbon, Kampakuya Naa Yakubu Abukari II, chiefs, elders and the people of the traditional area. He said the continued adherence to the Peace Accord, particularly its provision for the rotational selection of a successor between the Abudu and Andani royal families, was critical to safeguarding peace in the kingdom. “I am strongly encouraged by the decision of the Regent and senior traditional figures of Dagbon to uphold the Peace Accord, which has enshrined the time-tested traditions of Dagbon in selecting, through the principle of rotation, a worthy successor to Ya-Na Abukari II,” he said. According to the former President, the preservation of peace in Dagbon had implications far beyond the traditional area, stressing that stability in the kingdom was essential to the progress of northern Ghana and the country. “The peace of Dagbon is important not only to the people of Dagbon, but also to the peace, stability and development of the entire Northern sector and Ghana as a whole,” he said. Tribute to late Ya-Na Nana Akufo-Addo also paid tribute to the late Ya-Na Abukari II, whom he described as a friend, and commended his reign for its contribution to peace and development in Dagbon. The late Ya-Na died in July 2026, bringing to an end a reign that followed years of tension and conflict over the Dagbon chieftaincy. Following his death, Kampakuya Naa Yakubu Abukari II was installed as Regent in accordance with Dagbon customs. The former President’s visit formed part of efforts by leaders and stakeholders to honour the late Ya-Na and encourage the traditional authorities to maintain the peace that has characterised Dagbon in recent years. Nana Akufo-Addo’s call for continued adherence to the Peace Accord also comes at a sensitive period as the traditional area prepares for the processes leading to the selection and enskinment of a successor to the late Ya-Na.

items.title: Situation au Niger : L'AES salue la loyauté, le courage et le sens du devoir des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité nigériennes
items.description: Ceci est un communiqué de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES) relatif à la mutinerie survenue dans la ville de Niamey durant la nuit du 28 au 29 août 2026. La Confédération des États du Sahel (AES) a fait l'objet de trahison par un groupe de soldats impliqués dans une entreprise de déstabilisation à travers des attaques ayant ciblé la base aérienne 101 et certains sites sensibles dans la ville de Niamey au cours de la nuit du 28 au 29 août 2026. Grâce à la bravoure et au professionnalisme des forces républicaines loyalistes, cette nouvelle tentative a été contenue et mise en échec. La Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES) demeure pleinement engagée et mobilisée aux côtés du Niger dont elle partage la détermination à poursuivre la lutte pour la souveraineté et la paix. A cet effet, la Confédération AES : – réaffirme son soutien total aux institutions de la République du Niger ; – salue la loyauté, le courage et le sens du devoir des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité nigériennes qui, fidèles à leur serment, ont fait face à cette mutinerie et contribué au rétablissement de l'ordre ; – réaffirme sa détermination à préserver l'unité, la cohésion et la stabilité de la Confédération ; – invite les populations du Burkina Faso, de la République du Mali et de la République du Niger à rester particulièrement vigilantes face aux campagnes de désinformation, aux manipulations de l'opinion et aux tentatives de division susceptibles d'accompagner les entreprises de déstabilisation. Fait à Ouagadougou, le 29 août 2026 Pour les Porte-paroles des Gouvernements des Etats de la Confédération, le Porte-parole du Gouvernement du Burkina Pingdwendé Gilbert OUEDRAOGO

items.title: Ghana High Commission to UK steps in as stranded musician Barosky considers returning home
items.description: Ghanaian highlife musician Barosky has expressed his readiness to return to Ghana following an intervention by the Ghana High Commission in the United Kingdom to assess his welfare and explore ways of supporting him. The development follows public concern over the musician’s condition after a distressing video of him circulated widely on social media, prompting an outpouring of concern from Ghanaians in Ghana and abroad. The Ghanaian High Commissioner to the UK, Mrs Sabah Zita Benson, subsequently travelled to Manchester to meet Barosky and members of the Ghanaian community as part of efforts to determine how best to assist the veteran musician. Mrs Benson said the mission was initiated after the High Commission received several messages drawing attention to the video. “When the video came out, a lot of people forwarded it to us. So immediately, I instructed our consular office to reach out and see how we can resolve it,” she said. According to the High Commissioner, the decision to personally meet Barosky was informed by his contribution to Ghanaian music and the need for the Ghanaian community to rally around him. “Barosky has contributed immensely to Ghanaian music, and we all need to come together as a community to help him get back on his feet,” she said. Mrs Benson said the High Commission was willing to facilitate his return to Ghana should that be his preference. “So, I decided to make this move to hear from him and see how to help him settle, and, if he is willing to go home, we will assist him to do that,” Mrs Benson said. She stressed that restoring the musician’s wellbeing would require collective effort from the Ghanaian community. “Getting him back on his feet again means we must come together as a community and help him.” ‘Such a great talent’ The High Commissioner also paid tribute to Barosky’s musical talent, questioning why a musician of his calibre should be allowed to struggle without support. “Your talent was what shocked people. You are such a great talent, and how are we allowing it to go to waste?” she said. She explained that the Ghana High Commission continued to use the country’s creative and cultural industries to promote Ghana internationally. “We at the High Commission are promoting Ghana through arts, culture, music and food,” she added. The intervention has since offered Barosky an opportunity to consider returning home, with the musician indicating that he would be willing to return to Ghana if the necessary arrangements could be made. Barosky expressed appreciation to Mrs Benson and members of the Ghanaian community for their concern and support. The development has also renewed attention on the need to recognise and support veteran Ghanaian musicians whose contributions helped shape the country’s highlife tradition.

items.title: 2027: Thoroughly scrutinise Abiodun’s successor, Ogun monarch tells residents
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Eselu of Iselu Kingdom in Yewa North Local Government Area of Ogun State, Oba Akintunde Akinyemi, has urged residents of the State to thoroughly scrutinise all candidates seeking to succeed Governor Dapo Abiodun in the 2027 governorship election, irrespective of their political parties. The monarch also called on civil society organisations and the media to investigate the backgrounds, credentials and antecedents of the candidates before the election. Oba Akinyemi, who made the call while speaking with journalists on the sidelines of his house-warming ceremony at Obada-Oko area of Abeokuta, said the responsibility of choosing the next governor should not be left entirely to political parties, stressing that the electorate would ultimately bear the consequences of the choice made in 2027. He said, “let me use this opportunity to tell the electorate, civil society organisations and the press that whoever is going to become the next Governor of Ogun State after Dapo Abiodun should be thoroughly, and I mean thoroughly, scrutinised. “It is very important. We do not have another place to call our state. “Whoever wants to take over from the governor, irrespective of the political party, should be subjected to thorough scrutiny. The media and civil society organisations should come together to investigate all the candidates thoroughly, including their family backgrounds. It is very, very important.” The traditional ruler urged residents to ask critical questions about the individuals they intend to entrust with the leadership, governance and heritage of the state. “Everyone who belongs to this state has to ask questions. We must question whoever we plan to entrust with our heritage and governance,” he said. “This is no longer just about politics; it is about us and the critical stakeholders in the state. Everyone who belongs here must ensure that, if issues arise, we thoroughly understand the background and credentials of anyone who aspires to lead us.” Speaking on the internal crisis in the Ogun State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC), particularly the controversy surrounding the party’s primary election involving Senator Solomon Adeola and Hon. Abayomi Hunye, Oba Akinyemi urged the party leadership to intervene and resolve the matter amicably. The monarch expressed concern over what he described as the continuing agitation and counter-agitation arising from the dispute. “I have been following the trend of the news, including the agitation and counter-agitation. I think we have to implore the party to call them together and resolve whatever differences they may have,” he said. He questioned the controversy surrounding the votes allegedly recorded for Hunye during the primary election. “If Abayomi Hunye participated in the primaries, it is impossible for him to have scored zero votes because he would have at least voted for himself. So, who stole his vote?” he queried. “Even if the majority voted for Yayi, Hunye would not have cast his own vote for Yayi. Where did that single vote go?” According to him, the issue raises questions that require clarification, particularly regarding Hunye’s participation in the primary and the recording of his vote. “The core question is: what happened to his vote, and why was it not recorded? Had it been properly recorded, we might not be in this situation today,” he said. Oba Akinyemi advised the political actors involved to resolve their differences and avoid actions capable of unnecessarily heightening political tension, particularly on social media. “My advice to them is simple: put your house in order and stop unnecessarily overheating the polity on the internet,” he said. Speaking on the role of traditional rulers in politics, the monarch said traditional rulers must remain politically neutral while ensuring that the electorate carefully examines candidates before making its choice. “As traditional rulers in the state and having been on the throne for 21 years myself, our role is two-fold. First, we must remain neutral. Second, we must critically scrutinise every candidate, one by one. We must ensure that we do not make the wrong choice,” he said. “I implore all my fellow traditional rulers to exercise extreme care this time around and choose the right candidate.” On the agitation by the Yewa people for the governorship of Ogun State, Oba Akinyemi acknowledged the argument that the people had suffered political marginalisation, but said the overriding consideration should be the ability of the prospective governor to provide good governance. “Yes, the Yewa people are agitating for the governorship because we have been marginalised. That is an undeniable fact. However, our primary goal should remain securing a leader who will deliver good governance,” he said. He noted that political marginalisation was not peculiar to any particular ethnic group or region, stressing that the ultimate objective should be to elect a leader capable of delivering meaningful development to the people. “Regardless of background, my core focus is good governance. I want a leader who will deliver the dividends of democracy, prioritise basic education and empower our people. That is what is paramount to me. That is my prayer.” The post 2027: Thoroughly scrutinise Abiodun’s successor, Ogun monarch tells residents appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Affaire fosse commune d’Allassoyah: la CNDS monte au créneau, tient au respect des investigations judiciaires en cours, lance un appelle à la population et rassure que toute la lumière sera faite sur le dossier
items.description: Dans un communiqué rendu public ce samedi 29 août, la Commission nationale de Défense et de Sécurité (CNDS) a fait des mises au point relatives à la découverte de six corps sans vie dans la nuit du 23 au 24 août 2026 à Allassoyah, dans la préfecture de Forécariah. Aussitôt après l’annonce de cette nouvelle, ‘ ’le procureur de la République près le Tribunal de première instance de Forécariah, accompagné d’officiers de police judiciaire, s’est rendu sur les lieux afin d’effectuer les premières constatations. Les dépouilles ont ensuite été transférées à l’hôpital préfectoral de Forécariah pour les opérations d’identification et les examens nécessaires ’’, rappelle le communiqué du CNDS. Dans la foulée de cette action judiciaire entreprise sur le terrain à Forécariah, la Commission nationale de défense et de sécurité affirme avoir ‘’siégé en session extraordinaire le 28 août 2026, pour évaluer la situation générale. En outre, elle précise qu’ ‘’à ce stade, aucune conclusion définitive ne peut être tirée. En conséquence, elle s’abstient de toute déclaration ou interprétation, susceptible d’influencer les conclusions des investigations judiciaires en cours.’’ Afin d’éviter toute appréciation tendancieuse, la Commission Nationale de Défense et de Sécurité ‘’invite la population au calme, à la prudence et à la collaboration avec les services d’enquête ; appelle également à éviter toute spéculation ou diffusion d’informations, non vérifiées, susceptibles de perturber les investigations en cours’’. Enfin, la CNDS assure via son communiqué que ‘’toutes les dispositions nécessaires sont prises pour faire la lumière sur cette affaire et indique que les résultats des enquêtes seront communiqués par les canaux officiels, dès qu’ils seront disponibles.’’

items.title: North Korea defence minister sacked
items.description: North Korea’s defence minister has been dismissed as part of a reshuffle of the country’s military leadership, state media reported Sunday. The “structural reorganization plans” were decided during a meeting on Saturday led by Kim Jong Un, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. No Kwang Chol was not only dismissed as defence minister but also demoted in the ruling party leadership to “first vice-director of the Munitions Industry Department,” KCNA said. Kim Song Gi, director of the General Political Bureau of the Korean People’s Army, was named as the new defence minister. Another senior official, defence advisor Pak Jong Chon, was given the position of vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission and named to the ruling party’s Political Bureau. Several other promotions were also announced. The leadership shuffle comes shortly after joint annual drills between South Korea and the United States wrapped up. The drills, which are regularly denounced by Pyongyang as preparations for an invasion, were closely watched this year after US President Donald Trump ordered them to be shortened. Trump criticized the drills as provocative towards the North and bashed Seoul for not supporting his war against Iran. The US president also praised North Korean leader Kim, whom he met twice during his first term in office. AFP The post North Korea defence minister sacked appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Norway’s new king remembers ‘my dear father’ in first speech
items.description: King Haakon VIII of Norway has paid warm tribute to his late father, Harald V, in his first speech to the nation since taking the throne. “Thank you for being such a good dad,” he said in an at-times emotional televised address, seated at a desk in Norway’s royal palace, beside a picture of the late king, two lit candles and a bowl of white roses. Harald, 89, who was seen as a moderniser and “people’s king” during his 35-year reign, died in hospital on Friday morning after being treated for a rare blood condition. “Now it is my turn,” his 53-year-old son said, adding that a “major task” awaited him and that he wished to be “present and attentive” going forward. Haakon stressed national unity in the speech, saying the royal family believed in a “society built on law and justice, where everyone is of equal value”. He said Harald had been a good father to himself and his sister, Princess Märtha Louise, as well as a “warm and funny grandfather” to his six grandchildren and a “loving and caring husband” to his widow, Queen Sonja. The new king appeared to choke back tears as he noted that Saturday would have been their 58th wedding anniversary. Harald brought the family together “with a natural authority”, of which he might not have been aware himself, his son recalled. He had “always stayed true” to his “values and commitments”, the new king stressed. “He constantly reminded us in the family that each of us must do things in our own way. Find our own style. Be ourselves,” Haakon said. He also remarked on the “powerful and moving experience” of seeing thousands of Norwegians gather outside the royal palace in the capital Oslo with “flowers, tributes and candles”. “We are in mourning, yet at the same time it brings comfort and strength that so many are grieving together with us,” he said. Norwegians have been laying flowers outside the royal palace in Oslo since news broke that Harald had died on Friday. A national period of mourning has been declared, with no date yet given for his funeral. Among them was Norway’s Prime Minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, who laid flowers outside the palace and signed a book of condolences after greeting the new king, said the country was “united in grief and gratitude”. Haakon will swear an oath of allegiance in parliament on Tuesday and will later participate in a consecration service with his wife, Queen Mette-Marit – a stripped-down version of a coronation, which Norway no longer holds. He assumes his new role at a difficult time, as the royal family has faced health challenges and scandals this year. Mette-Marit came under scrutiny when it was revealed that she had had a three-year friendship with the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, for which she publicly apologised. She later received a lung transplant, after suffering from pulmonary fibrosis since 2018. Doctors will not declare her stable until next year, meaning her husband must balance his new official duties with her care. Her son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Høiby, was convicted in June of rape and other offences and sentenced to four years in prison. He is appealing. Høiby is not a member of the royal family, but was raised with them since he was four years old, when Haakon married his mother. Haakon’s sister, Märtha Louise, has also courted controversy for remarrying an American self-styled shaman in 2024, their business activities ultimately leading her to step back from royal duties. Without directly referencing these controversies, Haakon said during his speech: “Our family has experienced the importance of standing together in order to remain steadfast both within ourselves and for one another even during difficult times.” He said he, along with Mette-Marit and Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, would “always strive to understand the life situations of different people”. He added: “No one who lives in this country knows what we will face together, but what we do know is that we will stand by one another through both good days and difficult ones.” Although Harald remained popular until his death, a poll for newspaper Aftenposten earlier this year suggested that support for the monarchy had dropped from 72% in 2024 to 54%. However, Norwegian royal experts told the BBC that the new king, while facing questions about the turbulence surrounding his family, was respected, hard-working and, they believed, able to move forward despite the challenges.

items.title: 5 Fiscal Council members cleared
items.description: Parliament has approved five members nominated to serve on the Fiscal Council as part of government’s efforts to strengthen the country’s fiscal management and economic governance framework. The council is mandated to promote fiscal discipline, strengthen financial oversight and provide independent expert analysis to support sound decision-making in public financial management. Chaired by Dr Emmanuel Oteng Kumah, an international economic consultant and former board member of Standard Chartered Bank Ghana, the council is expected to play a key role in monitoring the implementation of the national budget and ensuring that government expenditure remains within sustainable limits. The move is also intended to contribute to long-term economic stability, in the wake of the country exiting the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme. President John Dramani Mahama nominated the five distinguished professionals to serve as members of the Fiscal Council on April 8 this year. The nominations are made pursuant to Section 11D of the Public Financial Management Act, 2016 (Act 921), as amended by the Public Financial Management (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act 1136). The establishment of the Fiscal Council is a strategic move by the government to reinforce the country’s economic framework. The council is tasked with strengthening financial oversight, ensuring fiscal prudence and providing independent expert analysis to shape sound decision-making in public financial management. The nominees represent a blend of academic excellence, research depth and seasoned policy experience. Members The other members are Professor Patrick Opoku Asuming, an academic and development economist at the University of Ghana Business School; Leslie Dwight Mensah, a representative of research think-tanks; J. Kweku Bedu-Addo, a former public policy expert at the Ministry of Finance, and Dr Henry Kofi Wampah, a former Governor of the Bank of Ghana. Adoption of report The approval of the nominees followed the presentation of the report of the Appointments Committee by its Chairman, Bernard Ahiafor. Mr Ahiafor urged the House to adopt the committee’s report on the President’s nominations for appointment as members of the Fiscal Council. He said the committee had recommended, by a majority decision of members present and voting, that the House approve the President’s nominees. Competent, qualified Seconding the motion, the Majority Leader, James Agalga, said all five nominees were highly competent and qualified to serve on the Council. The Majority Leader said Prof. Asuming was bringing an academic perspective to the council. “All the nominees, including Dr Henry Kofi Wampah, a former Governor of the Bank of Ghana, clearly have the expertise to serve in the capacity as members of the Fiscal Council,” he said. Mr Agalga, therefore, urged the House to approve the nominations. Consult gender partners On behalf of the House, the Speaker of Parliament, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, said the five nominees were qualified to serve on the Council and congratulated them on their appointment. “But I will draw your attention to the fact that it is a men’s club. As a gender advocate, I strongly urge them, in their deliberations, to always have some consultation with our gender partners. “It is very important as they have a lot of perspectives that we can benefit from. They should not be a men-only club as the Fiscal Council is for both men and women,” he said.

items.title: Kumuyi is a sage — Oyedepo says at crusade ground
items.description: Bishop David Oyedepo, Founder of Living Faith Church Worldwide, has described Pastor William Kumuyi as a sage whose ministry impacted lives globally. Oyedepo spoke on Saturday at the August edition of the Global Crusade with Kumuyi (GCK), with theme, ‘Total Transformation Through Christ,’ in Ota, Ogun. He said he had followed Kumuyi’s ministry from its early days and remained amazed by its strength, spiritual impact and influence. “This man is a sage. Today, I am amazed at the strength, the unction and the impact of this ministry all through these years,” he said. Oyedepo said he attended the crusade because “honour must be given to whom honour is due”, describing Kumuyi as a voice that had affected many globally. “May this grace continue to multiply, in the name of Jesus,” he prayed. He expressed confidence that participants would experience God’s grace throughout the programme, saying he expected remarkable things to happen. Oyedepo subsequently spoke on “How Shall We Escape, If We Neglect So Great a Salvation?”, stressing the importance of genuine salvation. Reading from Hebrews 2:3 and 2 Corinthians 13:5, he said salvation was not merely an ideology or belief but a tangible experience. “Salvation is not an ideology; it is an experience. May everyone gathered here tonight be set to experience the salvation of Christ,” he said. Oyedepo said his personal conversion was a definite experience, recalling that he gave his life to Christ on February 19, 1969, at the age of 15. “There was no guesswork. I knew what took place in my life when I did,” he said. He identified love, joy and peace as fruits that should characterise a regenerated life, urging Christians to examine their relationship with God. The cleric also urged believers to take spiritual responsibility by obeying God’s Word and maintaining their faith despite temptations. He stressed that reaching heaven required commitment and spiritual discipline because valuable things often came with a cost. “Everything of value carries a cost. Heaven is the most valuable destination. Therefore, there are definite costs,” he said. Kumuyi, while opening his sermon titled ‘The Great Transplanting of Blessings into Your Life’, praised Oyedepo’s steadfast faith. He said their relationship dated back to the 1970s, adding that they were renewing their fellowship and looking forward to greater things. “We enjoy one another fellowship as he and I are going younger at heart, we are re-establishing that fellowship, greater things are yet to come,” Kumuyi said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that one of the striking testimonies came from Mrs Florence Okafor, whose husband, Sunday, battled mental illness for 17 years. The testimony was among several accounts shared during the crusade, which entered its fourth day in Ota, with the grand finale scheduled for Sunday. (NAN) The post Kumuyi is a sage — Oyedepo says at crusade ground appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: L’appel pressant de Yankhoba Diémé
items.description: À quelques mois des prochaines échéances électorales, le parti présidentiel veut déjà occuper le terrain en Casamance. Ce samedi 29 août, Yankhoba Diémé a réuni les responsables de Kiiraay-Les Patriotes républicains de la Casamance autour d’un mot d’ordre : massifier, structurer et mobiliser pour gagner. ZIGUINCHOR – Pas question de laisser retomber la dynamique. Pour le troisième jour de sa tournée dans la région de Ziguinchor, le ministre des Forces armées et responsable du parti présidentiel dans le Sud a consacré sa journée aux responsables politiques de Kiiraay. Une rencontre placée sous le signe de l’écoute, de l’information et de la sensibilisation, mais surtout tournée vers la conquête du terrain. Tour à tour, les responsables politiques, parmi lesquels d’actuels et d’anciens maires de la Casamance, ont affiché leur détermination à investir les bases et à renforcer l’implantation de la nouvelle formation politique. Au cœur des échanges : la stratégie de massification, la mobilisation des militants et la structuration du parti en perspective des prochaines compétitions électorales. Face à ces leaders politiques, Yankhoba Diémé a appelé à l’ouverture et à l’unité. « Nous devons accueillir ceux qui nous rejoignent et leur donner toute leur place. Nous devons servir la Nation avec respect, humilité et responsabilité. Kiiraay doit être une maison ouverte à tous ceux qui veulent œuvrer pour la République », a-t-il déclaré. Mais le responsable politique a surtout mis en garde contre les divisions internes. « Vous avez fait naître un espoir et vous n’avez pas le droit de décevoir. Nous devons rester unis, travailler main dans la main et avancer ensemble vers la victoire. En Casamance, le seul adversaire de Kiiraay, c’est Kiiraay lui-même », a martelé l’enfant du département de Bignona, invitant « ses » troupes à garder « la construction du pays » comme boussole. Pour Yankhoba Diémé, l’heure est désormais à l’action. « Nous devons accélérer la massification, avec une véritable dynamique sur le terrain. Il faut occuper l’espace politique avec détermination et travailler comme un parti au pouvoir. Nous devons incarner la “Diomaye attitude” : travailler avec méthode, discrétion et efficacité, tout en restant généreux dans la parole », a-t-il lancé aux leaders ayant pris part à la rencontre. Son discours sonne comme une feuille de route pour les responsables de Kiiraay en Casamance : investir le terrain, renforcer les bases et transformer la dynamique politique en force électorale. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: MINURSO : un nouveau responsable onusien prend ses fonctions à Laâyoune
items.description: Un nouveau responsable onusien a rejoint la Mission onusienne au Sahara (MINURSO) à Laâyoune. Il s’agit de Ron Miste Kamwendo, originaire du Malawi, nommé directeur des affaires de la composante civile de la mission, dans le cadre des changements actuellement opérés au sein de sa structure administrative et fonctionnelle. Selon une source onusienne, Kamwendo est arrivé samedi à Laâyoune, où il a entamé les démarches liées à sa prise de fonction. Il succède à Jefferson Vinerand Mukamdoli, dont le mandat a pris fin à la suite de son départ à la retraite. Le nouveau responsable sera ainsi chargé des questions liées à la gestion et à l’accompagnement de la composante civile de la MINURSO. Cette fonction revêt une importance particulière pour le fonctionnement administratif et logistique de la mission, puisqu’elle implique la coordination des différents aspects liés à la composante civile et l’accompagnement de ses besoins, ainsi que la continuité du fonctionnement interne de la mission et la cohérence de ses dispositifs administratifs avec les exigences de la prochaine étape. La source de Hespress a souligné que l’arrivée du nouveau responsable onusien n’est liée à aucun changement dans le mandat politique de la MINURSO ni dans la nature de sa mission. Elle s’inscrit essentiellement dans le cadre du renouvellement habituel des responsabilités au sein de la composante civile de la mission, notamment après le départ à la retraite du précédent responsable et la nomination d’un nouveau cadre onusien à ce poste. Concernant les fonctions confiées à Kamwendo, la source a précisé qu’elles portent principalement sur la gestion de la composante civile et le suivi des aspects administratifs, organisationnels et logistiques liés au personnel de la mission, afin de garantir les conditions nécessaires à la poursuite de ses différentes activités sur le terrain et de son fonctionnement administratif. Ce changement intervient alors que la MINURSO poursuit ses missions au Sahara marocain, dans un contexte de maintien de la présence onusienne dans la région et de poursuite de la mise en œuvre de son mandat conformément aux résolutions du Conseil de sécurité. La composante civile constitue ainsi un élément essentiel de la structure opérationnelle permettant d’assurer la régularité et la continuité du travail de la mission. À noter que la MINURSO comprend, outre sa composante militaire, une composante civile chargée de plusieurs missions administratives, organisationnelles et logistiques. La mission onusienne reste soumise au mandat défini par le Conseil de sécurité, qui renouvelle périodiquement son mandat et fixe le cadre général de ses missions. The post MINURSO : un nouveau responsable onusien prend ses fonctions à Laâyoune appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: La Liga: Lookman scores as Atletico down Sevilla amid Alvarez distraction
items.description: Atletico Madrid put the noise of the Julian Alvarez transfer saga behind them with a convincing 3-1 victory at Sevilla on Saturday to move top of the early La Liga table. Diego Simeone’s men have taken seven points from their first three matches of the league season. The club has repeatedly ruled out a move to Barcelona for wantaway striker Alvarez, who has also been heavily linked with Arsenal. The Argentina international was left out of the matchday squad in Seville, having been booed by his own fans last weekend in a 2-2 home draw with Villarreal. The two forwards who started in his absence combined to great effect to give Atletico a fourth-minute lead. Lee Kang-in, a summer signing from European champions Paris Saint-Germain, played an excellent pass in behind for Alex Baena to rifle a low shot into the net. The Rojiblancos doubled their advantage in the 26th minute, as Ademola Lookman planted a clever shot inside Sevilla goalkeeper Odysseas Vlachodimos’s near post. Atletico were three goals in front just seven minutes later as Spanish World Cup winner Baena scored his second. Baena drove ashot into the bottom corner from outside the box after being teed up by Marcos Llorente. Sevilla improved in the second half and pulled one back through Miguel Sierra’s volley, but never looked like mounting a comeback. – Betis lose 100% record – Earlier, Real Betis lost their perfect start as Roger Brugue helped Levante to a 5-2 victory. Betis, whose fifth-place finish last term secured them a long-awaited return to the Champions League, would have gone top with a third win from as many outings to start their domestic campaign. But it was not to be for Manuel Pellegrini’s charges as goals from Adrian de la Fuente, Enzo Bardeli, Brugue and Jon Ander Olasagasti secured the hosts their first win of the season. De la Fuente broke the deadlock at the Ciutat de Valencia with a glancing header from a corner in the 24th minute. Shortly after the half-hour, former Barcelona centre-half Marc Bartra levelled for Betis with a forceful effort from the edge of the box. The match really sparked into life under the late summer Valencian sun as the clock ticked past 45 minutes. Bardeli displayed fantastic technique and imagination two minutes into added time as he pounced on a loose defensive pass and launched a chip from well over 40 yards that left Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles helpless. But the visitors managed to go into the break on level terms as Rodrigo Riquelme tucked in a flick-on from a corner. But a double from Brugue — the first another set-piece goal, before he bundled home from close range after Ivan Romero had struck the post — and a late Olasagasti header sealed the win. Real Sociedad got their first points of the season with a 2-1 home win over Espanyol. AFP The post La Liga: Lookman scores as Atletico down Sevilla amid Alvarez distraction appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Législatives à Laâyoune : une bataille à trois sièges s’annonce particulièrement disputée
items.description: Le cercle électoral de Laâyoune s’apprête à connaître une compétition acharnée entre les candidats et les partis politiques qui cherchent à décrocher ses sièges lors des prochaines élections législatives, ce qui devrait en faire l’une des principales circonscriptions électorales des provinces du Sud. Malgré les spécificités qui distinguent cette circonscription, à laquelle sont attribués trois sièges parlementaires, des autres circonscriptions du Royaume — en raison de sa situation géographique et de la portée politique et économique de la ville de Laâyoune, considérée comme la capitale des provinces du Sud —, l’intensité de la compétition électorale y reste également liée au poids du corps électoral, à l’influence des acteurs politiques ainsi qu’aux réseaux d’intérêts et aux ancrages sociaux qui jouent un rôle dans l’orientation des votes. 2021 : domination de l’Istiqlal et percée du RNI Les élections législatives de 2021 dans la circonscription de Laâyoune ont été marquées par l’obtention par le Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) d’un des trois sièges qui lui sont attribués, alors qu’il n’en détenait aucun lors des législatives de 2016. À l’inverse, le scrutin du 8 septembre 2021 a été marqué par l’échec du Parti de la justice et du développement (PJD) à conserver le siège qu’il avait obtenu en 2016. Son candidat, Mohamed Lamine Dida, n’a recueilli que 810 voix. La circonscription a, en revanche, confirmé la domination des Ouled Errachid sur le vote. Moulay Hamdi Ould Errachid, du Parti de l’Istiqlal, est arrivé en tête avec 47.548 voix, doublant ainsi le nombre de suffrages obtenus lors des élections de 2016. Le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) a lui aussi confirmé sa position, en arrivant deuxième. Son candidat, Sidi Mohammed Salem El Joumani, a obtenu 17.675 voix, conservant ainsi le siège décroché en 2016. Il a été suivi par le RNI, dont le candidat Mohamed Ayach a obtenu 8.198 voix, après l’échec du parti à décrocher un siège en 2016. Le candidat de l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP), Mohamed Errazma, n’est pas parvenu à obtenir de siège, avec 4.918 voix, suivi par le candidat du Mouvement populaire, Lahcen El Moutouakel, qui a obtenu 1.724 voix. Le PJD décroche un siège Lors des élections législatives de 2016, le Parti de l’Istiqlal, représenté par Moulay Hamdi Ould Errachid, avait obtenu un siège en arrivant en tête, avec près de 26.827 voix, alors que le taux de participation dans la circonscription avait atteint 57,12 %. Le PAM, qui avait présenté Sidi Mohammed Salem El Joumani, avait également remporté un siège en arrivant deuxième, avec 21.572 voix. Le PJD, représenté à l’époque par Brahim Daif, était arrivé troisième avec 8.424 voix, tandis que le candidat de l’USFP, Hassan Derhem, avait échoué à obtenir un siège après s’être classé quatrième avec 6.239 voix. Cette échéance électorale avait été marquée par la progression du PJD, malgré le maintien de la domination du Parti de l’Istiqlal, incarnée par Hamdi Ould Errachid, à Laâyoune, dont il préside le conseil communal. Ould Errachid et El Joumani « règnent » sur la circonscription de Laâyoune La carte électorale de la circonscription de Laâyoune n’a pas connu de changements majeurs, notamment concernant les premières places. Les figures traditionnelles bénéficiant d’un ancrage tribal et familial ont conservé leur position en tête, malgré les changements intervenus dans plusieurs autres circonscriptions. Entre 2016 et 2021, le Parti de l’Istiqlal a consolidé sa domination dans cette circonscription grâce à son candidat Hamdi Ould Errachid. Il a conservé le premier siège face aux candidats des autres formations politiques, tout en augmentant son nombre de voix entre les deux échéances. Ainsi, le « Parti de la balance » a presque doublé son score, passant de 26.827 voix en 2016 à 47.548 en 2021, arrivant largement en tête. Le PAM a, pour sa part, réussi à préserver sa position dans la capitale des provinces du Sud grâce à son candidat Sidi Mohammed Salem El Joumani, qui avait obtenu 21.572 voix en 2016, contre 17.675 en 2021. Le principal changement dans cette circonscription réside dans la chute du PJD et la perte de son troisième siège, qui est revenu au RNI, dont le candidat Mohamed Ayach a obtenu 8.198 voix. Les mêmes figures repartent au combat Pour la prochaine échéance électorale, plusieurs formations politiques ont choisi de miser sur les mêmes « joueurs » afin de préserver ou de renforcer leur position, ce qui devrait rendre la compétition particulièrement disputée dans la circonscription de Laâyoune, principale ville du Sahara marocain. Le nom de Hamdi Ould Errachid, membre du comité exécutif du Parti de l’Istiqlal, se distingue. Il a de nouveau été désigné pour conduire la liste électorale du parti dans cette circonscription, dans l’objectif de conserver son siège parlementaire et de maintenir le statu quo. Le PAM a suivi la même voie en investissant Sidi Mohammed Salem El Joumani comme tête de liste, dans l’objectif de conserver son siège parlementaire. L’USFP a, pour sa part, choisi de concourir pour le troisième siège en présentant Mouloud El Kirâa, considéré comme l’une des figures montantes de la scène politique locale à Laâyoune. Le RNI a également opté pour la continuité en annonçant la candidature du parlementaire sortant Mohamed Ayach à la tête de sa liste, afin de conserver son siège et de rivaliser avec les deux figures précitées. À cette compétition s’ajoutent le Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS), qui a investi Hassan Derhem, ainsi que le PJD, qui a choisi de présenter son coordinateur régional, Dadday Bibout. The post Législatives à Laâyoune : une bataille à trois sièges s’annonce particulièrement disputée appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
